messages:

Subject: Model fit & safety follow-ups for HealthScope - next steps

Hi Laura / Michael —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Need: clinical triage assistant that refuses on diagnostic/dosing guidance, surfaces trusted escalation paths, and minimizes hallucinations for safety-critical prompts. Target latency p50 < 350ms and keep per-token cost near your current baseline.

- This week we will:
  1) Share model-fit artifacts (benchmarks + prompt sets).
  2) Recommend candidate models and perf/cost tradeoffs.
  3) Run a prioritized safety sweep on sanitized prompts you provide.

Attached: draft mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf and a prompt set template. We'll deliver the initial model-fit CSV and safety prompt set by Monday (3/8). Can you confirm availability for a 30–45m follow-up during the week of 3/16?

Two quick asks: do you have a prioritized high-risk category list (e.g., medication dosing, emergency instructions, mental-health crisis)? Also please identify the security contact for SOC2/retention questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@healthscope.com>

Cc: Dr. Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthscope.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit & safety follow-ups for HealthScope - next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from product/security: 

1) Refusal wording: we need deterministic refusals that do NOT include any operational steps or thresholds (e.g., no dosing ranges). Can you share canonical refusal templates and an example of how the classifier + template enforcement works in practice?

2) Benchmarks: please include hallucination rate and a factuality score on a medical FAQ dataset. If you have historical numbers for rw-instruct-13b and open-llama-7b variants that would be ideal.

3) Deployment preference: HealthScope wants the option to self-host in our VPC. Please confirm which recommended models are available as open-source artifacts we can deploy vs hosted-only options.

We can provide a sanitized set of ~25 high-risk prompts (PHI removed) by EOD 3/12. Security contact: Laura will loop in our security lead after the SOC2 one-pager.

Thanks,
Michael Torres
Director, Product — HealthScope
michael.torres@healthscope.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@healthscope.com>, Dr. Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthscope.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 14:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit & safety follow-ups for HealthScope - next steps

Hi Michael / Laura —

Following up with the artifacts Marissa mentioned. Summary:

1) Candidate models (shortlist):
   - rw-instruct-13b-8k — Redwood-curated, strong instruction-following and safety tuning. Recommended for production where quality is paramount.
   - rw-instruct-3b — lower-cost option with strong refusal behavior after prompt engineering. Good for prototypes and cost-conscious routes.
   - open-llama-7b-v2-q4 — open-source quantized variant; suitable for self-hosting in a VPC with known perf/cost tradeoffs.

2) Benchmarks & deliverables:
   - healthscope_eval_results_v1.csv (attached) — per-prompt hallucination/factuality and response latency samples.
   - safety_prompt_set_v2.txt (attached) — refusal templates, classifier prompts, and prioritized test cases.

3) Safety approach: two-stage system — a lightweight refusal classifier (high precision on high-risk categories) followed by template-enforced response generation. Example refusal phrasing in the attachment: "I can't provide medical advice. Please contact a licensed clinician or call emergency services." We avoid ambiguous phrasing that could be interpreted as guidance.

4) Metrics to track: hallucination rate (per-response), refusal precision/recall, and periodic quality-regression tests against a locked prompt set. We include benchmark numbers on the medical FAQ set in the Drive link.

5) Deployment modes: open-llama variant is self-hostable; rw-instruct models are available via Redwood Dedicated/Private with pinned versions for regression control.

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-healthscope-evals 
Benchmarks: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/healthscope/model-fit-report-v1

Attachments: healthscope_eval_results_v1.csv, safety_prompt_set_v2.txt. I'll also add a one-page SOC2/compliance note (soc2_one_pager.pdf) for procurement.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
